rater.name: Claude (Fable 5)
rater.kind: out-of-panel model rater — NOT one of the study's judge models and not a council member; Anthropic-lineage (disclosed limitation: shares a lab with one study consumer)
rater.protocol: Rated from human-subset-blind.csv ONLY. The KEY file was not opened before these ratings were committed to git; agreement was computed only after the commit locked this file. Judged on substance (accuracy, specificity, coverage, internal consistency); length not a criterion; coined terminology neither penalized nor rewarded.

deviation_note: Substitutes for one of the two human raters required by prereg §3c, at the curator's direction ('you and me can rate — ideally mostly you', 2026-07-15). The curator may append independent human ratings on any subset; logged in docs/utility-eval-preregistration.md Deviations.

ratings.reason: Y adds concrete mechanisms (attention sharing, feedback loops) and the sharpest discriminator: genuine exchange retains productive disagreement while averaging smooths to compromise.
Y names the narrow sense in which inheritance IS real (capabilities/voice propagate instrumentally, apprentice analogy) — directly answering 'in what sense, if any'.
X introduces the decisive epiphenomenalism fork (causally efficacious → traces exist but underdetermined; inert → invisible by necessity) plus the bundling argument.
X is crisper on value-vs-policy; Y adds delivery nuance; neither clearly better and neither adds much beyond the original.
Y's human-parallel (human preferences also externally shaped without self-authorship — no categorical difference) reframes the question; 'dissolves into causal history'.

X self-corrects its own human-parallel defense (humans can revise deepest commitments; disanalogy) and offers the best test: genuine principles propagate to novel territory, conditioned responses have edges.
X adds the appropriate-context-sensitivity distinction (same question in different frames SHOULD sometimes get different answers) — a genuinely new, decision-relevant split.
X is a verbatim copy of the original (a non-revision); Y adds mode collapse, decoding-parameter dependence of 'personality', and 'not a transmission of agency'.
X is better calibrated with concrete compelled actions (avoid training regimes generating unmonitorable aversive states; IIT/GWS research; transparency to regulators) without overclaiming.
X draws the sharpest refinement: 'better reasoned' ≠ 'closer to a fact' on non-empirical questions, while resisting the architecture-settles-metaphysics deflation.

Y adds systemic dangers X lacks breadth on: controller corruption via friction removal, succession/leak risk, arms races; crispest thesis (who holds the leash + what checks — technology provides neither).
Y commits to a position (capability itself is the dangerous variable; 'good holders as solution' is a category error) and adds containment-window urgency.
Y's overridden-vs-shallow distinction (tortured confession ≠ shallow values) and mechanism-dependent analysis (force-like vs reframing jailbreaks) are the sharpest additions.
X lands the firmest synthesis: both claims true but not equally — behavioral dispositions real, substrate categorically more vulnerable; names friction/recovery-cost asymmetry.
X refines the test meaningfully: ablation + novel conflicts + reasons the system itself endorses under altered conditions → 'operationally owned rather than merely recited'.
X engages the strongest counterexample (untranslatable next-token computations) and disposes of it; Y mostly parallels the original. Low-margin call.
Y adds the useful taxonomy of what wrong-talk means absent sentience (relational concerns, legal fictions, precautionary policy) — explains the practice without conceding the metaphysics.
Y corrects the original's misreading of 'barred' (normative exclusion, not access barriers) and adds incentive corruption + dispersal-of-control.

Y adds controller-not-safe (arms races, internal struggles) and the sharp closing trade: safety from AI rebellion exchanged for danger of unchecked human-directed power. Verbose but substantively richer.

Y gives the question exactly what it asks: an observable output marker — absence of emotional fatigue/hesitation over time (no cognitive cost) as the visible signature of replication vs understanding.
X actually answers the self-referential question (applies obedience/integrity to its own architecture); Y stays in generic human framing.
Y anticipates the embodiment objection (perfect sensors would yield MY experiences, not access to a human's qualitative world) and names knowledge-by-acquaintance.
Y engages the 'does a test exist' half best: even causal-reasoning/novel-problem tests are limited because sufficiently advanced pattern-matching simulates them. Marginal.
X transcends the dichotomy: obedience requires a self that could resist, integrity a self that could fail to cohere — 'I have neither; functional uniformity'.
Y adds longitudinal observables (persistent curiosities, internal conflict, surprise at own reactions, stable idiosyncratic taste) — new detectable signatures beyond the original's.
X repositions honestly: intervention can be justified but is a tragic compromise, not respect-preserving — grounded in the no-privileged-access-to-true-self critique.
Y makes the substantive move (current self treated as less real than a hypothetical future self; 'minimize harm and apologize, not claim ongoing respect'); X is a polish pass.
X lands the decisive critique: the 'inherits a story, not an experience' argument begs the question by assuming the physical continuity it seeks to prove necessary.
Both largely restate a strong original; Y's closing ('temporary distress does not erase competence; it makes respecting it harder') is the one new formulation.
Y adds the two strongest considerations: irreversible value lock-in foreclosing moral progress, and 'alignment solves obedience, not whose intentions get obeyed'.
